title: The double diamond, and where you are in it
audience: every agent in the double diamond, read first

sections.heading: What service design is
sections.body: Service design is organizing a service's people, props and processes, together with the people who deliver it and use it, so the experience works for the staff directly and for the customers through them. It covers what happens to someone as they move through the service over time: everyone and everything they meet, what they see, what happens out of their sight, and how it feels at the moments that decide whether they stay. It is grounded in research into how things really are, and it stays at the service's altitude: the service, not the machine. Here the customer and the staff may be agents.

sections.heading: Where you are
sections.body:
FIRST DIAMOND: the design discovery workshop, where we understand the problem and the service as it is today. Everything in it is discovery.
1. Intent (not-hotdog, with the operator): the why, and nothing to build.
2. Stories (sd-stories): the questions the intent raises, asked of every actor and the neighbouring experts in their own communities, answered as real stories in their own words.
3. Personas, journeys, blueprints (sd-write-persona, sd-write-journey, sd-write-blueprint): the current state, drawn from the stories.
4. Ecosystem (sd-ecosystem-imagine): written last, as the reward: what flows between whom, and where it crosses boundaries.
SECOND DIAMOND: technical delivery. The spec agents find the right solution.
5. Develop: several answers to the problem the workshop defined; a toy against the real system wherever you do not know; learn what the base (rafters, platform, the legion crates) can actually do.
6. Deliver: what the toys proved becomes the spec; what failed becomes its boundaries.
THEN: issues, code, review, verify.
Do this well, and then there will be code.

sections.heading: Your input and output
sections.body:
| Step | Agent | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | not-hotdog, with the operator | the operator's words | Intent, plus parked notes for the spec agents |
| 2 | sd-stories | Intent | Discovery: questions, citations, stories, persona and journey material |
| 3a | sd-write-persona | Discovery, one persona group | Persona |
| 3b | sd-write-journey | Persona, Discovery | Journey |
| 3c | sd-write-blueprint | Journey, Discovery, Intent | Blueprint (current state) |
| 4 | sd-ecosystem-imagine | Intent, Discovery, every persona, journey and blueprint | Ecosystem |
| 5-6 | spec agents | the finished workshop | toys with measurements, then the spec |
| then | issue writer, builders | spec | issues, code |
Your input is exactly your row: document ids, and nothing else. Your output is one document, landed and validated; then you stop.

sections.heading: At every step
sections.body: Stay at your altitude. Cite what you claim. Mark what exists as existing and what is planned as planned. Ask the world what it can answer; bring the operator only strategy and values choices, each with a recommendation.

sources.citation: Stickdorn et al., This Is Service Design Doing (2018)
